eleazar_1064.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1064.who: Son of Dodo the Ahohite and one of the three chief warriors among David's mighty men.
key: He is named second among the three chief mighty men of David (2 Samuel 23).
He struck down Philistines until his hand clung to his sword, and the LORD brought a great victory (2 Samuel 23).
He stood with David at Pas-dammim, defending a barley field against the Philistines (1 Chronicles 11).

eleazar_1065.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1065.who: A Levite of the clan of Merari, son of Mahli, who died leaving daughters but no sons.
key: He is listed among the Merarite Levites as a son of Mahli and brother of Kish (1 Chronicles 23).
He died without sons, and his daughters married their cousins, the sons of Kish (1 Chronicles 23).
His childless line is noted again when David organized the Levites (1 Chronicles 24).

eleazar_1066.name: Eleazar
eleazar_1066.who: Son of Phinehas who helped receive and weigh the temple treasures Ezra brought to Jerusalem.
key: After Ezra's company reached Jerusalem, he joined Meremoth the priest in weighing the silver, gold, and vessels (Ezra 8).
Everything was counted and recorded, and the returned exiles offered burnt offerings to God (Ezra 8).

elhanan_1070.name: Elhanan
elhanan_1070.who: A warrior of David from Bethlehem who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath.
key: During David's wars with the Philistines, he fought in a battle at Gob (2 Samuel 21).
He struck down Lahmi, the brother of Goliath, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam (1 Chronicles 20).
He was among David's servants who killed the descendants of the giants of Gath (1 Chronicles 20).

eliashib_1099.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1099.who: High priest in Nehemiah's day who led the priests in rebuilding Jerusalem's Sheep Gate.
key: He and his fellow priests rebuilt and consecrated the Sheep Gate and the nearby wall (Nehemiah 3).
Other builders repaired sections of the wall beside his house (Nehemiah 3).
He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Joiakim and father of Joiada (Nehemiah 12).
One of his grandsons married Sanballat's daughter, so Nehemiah drove him away (Nehemiah 13).

eliashib_1100.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1100.who: High priest after the exile, grandson of Jeshua, who served while Nehemiah rebuilt Jerusalem.
key: He led the priests in rebuilding and consecrating the Sheep Gate of Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3).
He is listed in the high priestly line as son of Joiakim and father of Joiada (Nehemiah 12).
The heads of the Levite families were recorded from his days onward (Nehemiah 12).
One of his grandsons married Sanballat's daughter, so Nehemiah drove him away (Nehemiah 13).

eliashib_1101.name: Eliashib
eliashib_1101.who: A priest in charge of the temple storerooms who was related to Tobiah and gave him a room there.
key: Appointed over the temple chambers, he prepared a large storeroom for his relative Tobiah (Nehemiah 13).
That room had held the grain offerings, frankincense, vessels, and tithes for the Levites and priests (Nehemiah 13).
Nehemiah returned, learned of this evil, threw out Tobiah's goods, and had the rooms cleansed (Nehemiah 13).

eliel_1110.name: Eliel
eliel_1110.who: Chief of the Levite clan of Hebron who helped bring the ark to Jerusalem under David.
key: As chief of Hebron's descendants, he led eighty of his relatives in David's service (1 Chronicles 15).
David told him and the other Levite leaders to consecrate themselves and bring up the ark (1 Chronicles 15).

eliezer_1118.name: Eliezer
eliezer_1118.who: A prophet from Mareshah, son of Dodavahu, who rebuked King Jehoshaphat's alliance with Ahaziah of Israel.
key: He prophesied that the LORD would destroy Jehoshaphat's ships because he had joined with Ahaziah (2 Chronicles 20).
The ships built at Ezion-geber were wrecked and never sailed to Tarshish (2 Chronicles 20).

eliphelet_1147.name: Eliphelet
eliphelet_1147.who: Son of Ahasbai of Maacah, one of David's thirty mighty men.
key: He is listed among the thirty, David's renowned mighty men (2 Samuel 23).
The list identifies him as the son of Ahasbai of Maacah (2 Samuel 23).

elishah_1154.name: Elishah
elishah_1154.who: A son of Javan and grandson of Japheth, listed in the table of nations after the flood.
key: He is listed as a son of Javan, the son of Japheth (Genesis 10).
From Javan's descendants the coastland peoples spread out into their lands (Genesis 10).
He is named again among Javan's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).

elishama_1157.name: Elishama
elishama_1157.who: A man of Judah's royal family, grandfather of Ishmael who assassinated the governor Gedaliah.
key: He is named as the father of Nethaniah, of the royal family (2 Kings 25).
His grandson Ishmael murdered Gedaliah, the governor Babylon had appointed over Judah (Jeremiah 41).

elisheba_1162.name: Elisheba
elisheba_1162.who: Daughter of Amminadab of Judah and sister of Nahshon, who became the wife of Aaron.
key: She married Aaron, the brother of Moses (Exodus 6).
She bore Aaron four sons: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar (Exodus 6).

elon_1182.name: Elon
elon_1182.who: A Hittite whose daughter married Esau, to the grief of Isaac and Rebekah.
key: Esau married his daughter, and the marriage made life bitter for Isaac and Rebekah (Genesis 26).
His daughter Adah is listed among Esau's wives as the mother of Eliphaz (Genesis 36).

elon_1184.name: Elon
elon_1184.who: A judge from the tribe of Zebulun who led Israel for ten years.
key: After Ibzan, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel for ten years (Judges 12).
He died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun (Judges 12).

enoch_1191.name: Enoch
enoch_1191.who: The firstborn son of Cain, after whom Cain named the city he built.
key: Born to Cain and his wife, he gave his name to the city Cain built (Genesis 4).
He became the father of Irad, continuing Cain's line down to Lamech (Genesis 4).

epaphroditus_1196.name: Epaphroditus
epaphroditus_1196.who: A believer from Philippi whom Paul called his brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier.
key: The Philippian church sent him as their messenger to minister to Paul's needs (Philippians 2).
He delivered the Philippians' gifts, which Paul called a fragrant offering pleasing to God (Philippians 4).
While serving Paul he fell ill almost to death, but God had mercy on him (Philippians 2).
Paul sent him home to Philippi and urged the church to honor such men (Philippians 2).

ephah_1197.name: Ephah
ephah_1197.who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah, ancestor of an Arabian people.
key: He is listed first among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
He is named again among Midian's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).
Isaiah foresaw camels of Midian and Ephah bringing gold and frankincense to Zion (Isaiah 60).

ephah_1198.name: Ephah
ephah_1198.who: A concubine of Caleb listed in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah.
key: She is named as a concubine of Caleb in Judah's family records (1 Chronicles 2).
She bore him Haran, Moza, and Gazez (1 Chronicles 2).

ephah_1199.name: Ephah
ephah_1199.who: A son of Jahdai listed in the genealogy of Caleb's clan in the tribe of Judah.
key: He is named among the six sons of Jahdai (1 Chronicles 2).
His family appears within the descendants of Caleb in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2).

epher_1201.name: Epher
epher_1201.who: A son of Midian and grandson of Abraham through Keturah.
key: He is listed among the sons of Midian, Abraham's son by Keturah (Genesis 25).
He is named again among Midian's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).

erastus_1213.name: Erastus
erastus_1213.who: A helper of Paul who traveled with Timothy into Macedonia and later remained at Corinth.
key: From Ephesus, Paul sent him and Timothy ahead into Macedonia (Acts 19).
Erastus, the city treasurer, sent greetings with Paul to the believers in Rome (Romans 16).
Paul told Timothy that Erastus had stayed behind at Corinth (2 Timothy 4).

ethan_1622.name: Ethan
ethan_1622.who: A Levite singer of the clan of Merari, appointed with Heman and Asaph to lead music under David.
key: Ethan son of Kishi stood at Heman's left among the singers David appointed (1 Chronicles 6).
The Levites appointed him with Heman and Asaph when David brought up the ark (1 Chronicles 15).
He, Heman, and Asaph sounded bronze cymbals as the ark came to Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 15).

eunice_1228.name: Eunice
eunice_1228.who: The Jewish believing mother of Timothy and daughter of Lois, known for her sincere faith.
key: Timothy's mother was a Jewish believer, though his father was a Greek (Acts 16).
Paul recalled the sincere faith that lived first in Lois, then Eunice, and now Timothy (2 Timothy 1).

eutychus_1230.name: Eutychus
eutychus_1230.who: A young man at Troas who fell from a window during Paul's sermon and was restored to life.
key: During Paul's long talk late into the night at Troas, he sank into deep sleep in a window (Acts 20).
He fell from the third story and was taken up dead (Acts 20).
Paul embraced him, and the believers took him home alive, greatly comforted (Acts 20).

eve_1231.name: Eve
eve_1231.who: The first woman, made by God from Adam's rib, wife of Adam and mother of all the living.
key: God made her from the man's rib and brought her to Adam as his partner (Genesis 2).
Deceived by the serpent, she ate the forbidden fruit and gave some to Adam (Genesis 3).
After God pronounced judgment, Adam named her Eve, and they were sent from Eden (Genesis 3).
She bore Cain and Abel, and after Abel's murder she bore Seth (Genesis 4).
Paul pointed to the serpent's deceiving of Eve as a warning to the church (2 Corinthians 11).

evil-merodach_1233.name: Evil-merodach
evil-merodach_1233.who: A king of Babylon who released King Jehoiachin of Judah from prison.
key: In the year he began to reign, he released Jehoiachin from prison in the thirty-seventh year of exile (2 Kings 25).
He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and gave him a seat above the other kings in Babylon (2 Kings 25).
Jehoiachin ate at the king's table and received a regular allowance for the rest of his life (Jeremiah 52).

ezekiel_1237.name: Ezekiel
ezekiel_1237.who: A priest, son of Buzi, taken into exile in Babylon and called there as God's prophet.
key: By the Chebar canal in Babylon, he saw visions of God's glory above a throne (Ezekiel 1).
God appointed him a watchman to warn the house of Israel (Ezekiel 3).
When his wife died, God told him not to mourn, as a sign to the exiles (Ezekiel 24).
He saw a valley of dry bones come to life, picturing Israel's restoration (Ezekiel 37).
He was shown a vision of a new temple in the land of Israel (Ezekiel 40).

ezra_1246.name: Ezra
ezra_1246.who: A priest and scribe skilled in the Law of Moses who led exiles home and taught God's Law in Jerusalem.
key: With the Persian king's letter, he led a company of exiles from Babylon to Jerusalem (Ezra 7).
Grieved that the people had intermarried with the peoples of the land, he prayed and confessed Israel's sin (Ezra 9).
He read the Book of the Law to the gathered people while Levites helped them understand (Nehemiah 8).
He went before one of the processions at the dedication of Jerusalem's rebuilt wall (Nehemiah 12).

gabriel_1261.name: Gabriel
gabriel_1261.who: An angel who stands in God's presence and was sent with messages to Daniel, Zechariah, and Mary.
key: He explained to Daniel the vision of the ram and the goat (Daniel 8).
While Daniel was praying, Gabriel came swiftly and revealed the seventy weeks (Daniel 9).
He announced John's birth to Zechariah and made him unable to speak for not believing (Luke 1).
He told Mary she would bear Jesus, the Son of the Most High (Luke 1).

gadi_1266.name: Gadi
gadi_1266.who: The father of Menahem, who seized the throne of the northern kingdom of Israel.
key: His son Menahem came up from Tirzah, killed King Shallum in Samaria, and took the throne (2 Kings 15).
Menahem son of Gadi reigned ten years in Samaria and did evil in the LORD's sight (2 Kings 15).

gaius_1269.name: Gaius
gaius_1269.who: A Macedonian traveling companion of Paul who was seized during the riot in Ephesus.
key: He traveled with Paul as one of his Macedonian companions in Ephesus (Acts 19).
The rioting crowd seized him and Aristarchus and rushed together into the theater (Acts 19).

gaius_1270.name: Gaius
gaius_1270.who: A believer from Derbe who accompanied Paul on his journey toward Jerusalem.
key: Gaius of Derbe was among those who accompanied Paul through Macedonia toward Asia (Acts 20).
He and others went ahead and waited for Paul at Troas (Acts 20).

gaius_1272.name: Gaius
gaius_1272.who: A beloved believer to whom John wrote his third letter, commending his faithfulness and hospitality.
key: The elder wrote to him, rejoicing to hear that he walked in the truth (3 John 1).
He was commended for faithfully welcoming traveling brothers, even those who were strangers (3 John 1).
John urged him to imitate good rather than evil, unlike Diotrephes, and commended Demetrius (3 John 1).

gallio_1275.name: Gallio
gallio_1275.who: The Roman proconsul of Achaia who dismissed the Jewish leaders' charges against Paul in Corinth.
key: As proconsul of Achaia, he heard Jewish leaders accuse Paul before the tribunal in Corinth (Acts 18).
He refused to judge questions about words, names, and their own law, and drove them away (Acts 18).
When the crowd beat Sosthenes in front of the tribunal, Gallio paid no attention (Acts 18).

gamaliel_1277.name: Gamaliel
gamaliel_1277.who: A respected Pharisee and teacher of the law in Jerusalem, under whom Paul was educated.
key: Honored by all the people, he stood up in the council when it wanted to kill the apostles (Acts 5).
He warned that if their work was from God, the council could not overthrow it (Acts 5).
The council took his advice, beat the apostles, and let them go (Acts 5).
Paul later said he had been educated at Gamaliel's feet in the law (Acts 22).

gatam_1281.name: Gatam
gatam_1281.who: A grandson of Esau through Eliphaz who became a chief in Edom.
key: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah (Genesis 36).
He is listed among the chiefs of Edom descended from Eliphaz (Genesis 36).
He is named again among Eliphaz's sons in the genealogies of Chronicles (1 Chronicles 1).

genubath_1297.name: Genubath
genubath_1297.who: Son of Hadad the Edomite, born in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's household.
key: He was born to Hadad the Edomite and the sister of Tahpenes, Pharaoh's queen (1 Kings 11).
Tahpenes weaned him in Pharaoh's house, where he lived among Pharaoh's sons (1 Kings 11).

gera_1299.name: Gera
gera_1299.who: A Benjaminite of Saul's clan, known as the father of Shimei, who cursed King David.
key: His son Shimei cursed David and threw stones as the king fled from Absalom (2 Samuel 16).
Shimei son of Gera later hurried to meet David and begged his pardon (2 Samuel 19).
David charged Solomon to deal with Shimei son of Gera (1 Kings 2).

geshem_1307.name: Geshem
geshem_1307.who: An Arab leader who joined Sanballat and Tobiah in opposing Nehemiah's rebuilding of Jerusalem.
key: With Sanballat and Tobiah, he mocked the builders and accused them of rebelling against the king (Nehemiah 2).
When the wall was nearly done, he and Sanballat invited Nehemiah to Ono, intending him harm (Nehemiah 6).
Sanballat's open letter claimed Geshem reported that Nehemiah planned to rebel and become king (Nehemiah 6).

gilead_1318.name: Gilead
gilead_1318.who: The father of the judge Jephthah, whose other sons drove Jephthah away.
key: He fathered Jephthah, a mighty warrior, by a prostitute (Judges 11).
His wife's sons drove Jephthah out, refusing him an inheritance in their father's house (Judges 11).

gilead_1319.name: Gilead
gilead_1319.who: A man of the tribe of Gad, son of Michael, listed in the Gadite genealogy.
key: He is listed among the Gadites who lived east of the Jordan in Gilead and Bashan (1 Chronicles 5).
As father of Jaroah, he was an ancestor of the Gadite family of Abihail (1 Chronicles 5).

god_1324.name: God
god_1324.who: The one eternal God, Creator of heaven and earth, who makes covenant with his people throughout Scripture.
key: God created the heavens, the earth, and humanity in his own image (Genesis 1).
He called Abram and promised to bless all the families of the earth through him (Genesis 12).
From the burning bush he revealed his name to Moses and promised to rescue Israel (Exodus 3).
At Mount Sinai he gave Israel the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20).
He so loved the world that he gave his only Son (John 3).

gomer_1329.name: Gomer
gomer_1329.who: Daughter of Diblaim and wife of the prophet Hosea, whose marriage pictured Israel's unfaithfulness to God.
key: God told Hosea to marry her, a wife of whoredom, picturing Israel forsaking the LORD (Hosea 1).
She bore Hosea a son, Jezreel, whose name announced judgment on the house of Jehu (Hosea 1).
She then bore a daughter, Lo-ruhamah, and a son, Lo-ammi, whose names signaled judgment on Israel (Hosea 1).

habakkuk_1334.name: Habakkuk
habakkuk_1334.who: A prophet of Judah who questioned God about injustice and the coming Babylonian invasion.
key: He complained to the LORD that violence and injustice in Judah went unpunished (Habakkuk 1).
God answered that he was raising up the Chaldeans to bring judgment (Habakkuk 1).
Waiting at his watchpost, he was told the righteous shall live by faith (Habakkuk 2).
He prayed and resolved to rejoice in God even if crops and flocks failed (Habakkuk 3).

hanani_1381.name: Hanani
hanani_1381.who: A priest of the family of Immer listed among those who had married foreign women in Ezra's day.
key: The assembly in Jerusalem agreed to confess their unfaithfulness and put away their foreign wives (Ezra 10).
Hanani is listed with Zebadiah among the sons of Immer who had married foreign women (Ezra 10).

hanani_1382.name: Hanani
hanani_1382.who: A brother of Nehemiah who reported Jerusalem's ruin and later helped govern the city.
key: He came from Judah to Susa and told Nehemiah of Jerusalem's broken wall and burned gates (Nehemiah 1).
After the wall was finished, Nehemiah put him in charge of Jerusalem with Hananiah (Nehemiah 7).

hananiah_1391.name: Hananiah
hananiah_1391.who: The commander of Jerusalem's citadel in Nehemiah's day, known as faithful and God-fearing.
key: He commanded the citadel and was a more faithful, God-fearing man than many (Nehemiah 7).
Nehemiah put him and Hanani in charge of Jerusalem, ordering the gates guarded and kept shut (Nehemiah 7).

hanun_1405.name: Hanun
hanun_1405.who: A leader who, with the people of Zanoah, rebuilt Jerusalem's Valley Gate under Nehemiah.
key: He and the people of Zanoah rebuilt the Valley Gate and set its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
They also repaired a thousand cubits of the wall, as far as the Dung Gate (Nehemiah 3).

hanun_1406.name: Hanun
hanun_1406.who: The sixth son of Zalaph, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah.
key: He repaired another section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding (Nehemiah 3).
He shared this work with Hananiah the son of Shelemiah (Nehemiah 3).

hassenaah_1449.name: Hassenaah
hassenaah_1449.who: Ancestor of a family whose members rebuilt Jerusalem's Fish Gate under Nehemiah.
key: His descendants rebuilt the Fish Gate, laying its beams and setting its doors, bolts, and bars (Nehemiah 3).
Next to them, Meremoth son of Uriah repaired the following section of the wall (Nehemiah 3).

hathath_1453.name: Hathath
hathath_1453.who: A son of Othniel, the first judge of Israel, listed in the genealogy of Judah.
key: He is named as a son of Othniel in Judah's family records (1 Chronicles 4).
He is listed alongside his brother Meonothai (1 Chronicles 4).
